criteria.name: Thumb-stop cover
criteria.why: 'One award per state. Alaska is 552 Rhode Islands.' is a best-in-class LinkedIn cover line: 9 words, a specific number, a named tension, no jargon, and visibly Alaskan through a genuinely well drawn relief map rather than an aurora cliche. Verified legible at 432px in slide-01-thumb.png. Two real costs. The headline set on THREE lines at 111.5px, not the two its own dossier declared and its acceptance checklist required, which drops the type size and pushes the mass down. And the cover's declared wordless claim, two identical 48px rings on two wildly different grounds, does not survive the feed: at 432px the ring on Alaska is a faint pink thread and the Rhode Island chip is a smudge with a stray unlabelled leader running off it. The headline carries the slide alone. Large dead region through the mid-left.

criteria.name: Story arc & swipe momentum
criteria.why: Genuinely composed as a sequence, not a list. S02 delivers the cover's loop instantly by applying the rule to all fifty states at once. S03 escalates with the rule verbatim plus its enforcement half. The breather lands correctly at S05, and handing the whole frame to NSF's own sentence at the exact moment the argument turns is the deck's best structural decision. S07 makes NSF's case properly before declining it, which is what earns the disagreement. S08 stops arguing and becomes useful. The neatline margin, the NN/09 counter and the projection-note state machine make the contact sheet read as one sheet. Deduction: S02 and S06 are two tellings of the same picture, fifty states at true relative area wearing identical rings, and S06 is the weaker drawing of the two, so one beat is redundant rather than reorderable. The flow critic's own pre-fix read was 7.0.

criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.why: The declared attack partly worked and must be credited: eleven named techniques with none on more than four slides, drawn share 66 percent, median pairwise similarity 0.329, and three surfaces that genuinely survive the zoom test. S05's hachure field has real varied stroke width across four accumulated passes and true tonal depth; S07's and S01's Alaska resolve ridges, valleys, the full Aleutian chain and the Southeast panhandle; S08's 82 engraved day ticks with every seventh heavier is data as texture. S04's casting is a real modelled solid with a measured contact shadow at dL 21.8. That is a real move off the 6.0 this criterion has scored in 7 of the last 10 runs. It is not 8, for five specific reasons. FIRST, one organic hair texture supplies the visual signature on six of nine slides and is the wrong material on most of them: it is the bottom band on 01, 02, 06 and 09, the whole field on 05, and the surface of the funding casting on 04, where the dossier explicitly promised metal that 'reads machined rather than organic' and shipped what reads as shag. The bench has eleven techniques but ONE texture carries the deck's look, which is the exact failure mode the plan set out to kill, arriving through the back door. SECOND, the deck's headline physics claim, ONE GLOBAL LIGHT at azimuth 118 elevation 26 from a single declared constant, is false on its two best-crafted slides: AK.reliefShade runs its own NW key on 01 and 07 and it is visible. Disclosed, but disclosure does not buy it back. THIRD, S03's declared rescue from deliberate flatness, engraved registration furniture with lit inner edges and cast shadows plus a ghost coastline running down through the band, shipped as 1px line art; the region y1250 to y1600 is the deck's largest dead zone. FOURTH, S07 fails its own acceptance checklist item, 'Alaska's relief mass is cut by the bottom edge, not floating above it' -- it floats, above an empty band. FIFTH, S09's sheet does not read as lifted off a table (side face invisible, deckle on one edge only) and its Alaska is a bare outline where the dossier declared the deck's last engraved surface. Of the three structural commitments, the bench delivered, the drawn share delivered at 66 against a 65 target, and 'the bottom band is designed first' delivered on 04, 05 and 08 and reduced to texture-plus-type on 02, 03, 06, 07 and 09. Flat is argued honestly in the dossier, so the rendered-ladder clause is satisfied.

criteria.name: Story-art fusion
criteria.why: The deck's strongest dimension and unusually rigorous. The 48px invariant ring IS claim C01 drawn as an object, meaningful only through what sits under it. Alaska and Rhode Island run through one d3.geoConicEqualArea, so the 552 ratio is COMPUTED and draws itself rather than being illustrated. On S04 the volume between the $40M and $100M scribe lines is deliberately left unfilled because a range is a range, which is claims C10 and C11 refusing to assert a number NSF does not state, and the $100M scribe is machine-asserted at 460 vs 460 px. Ten countable rings equal C12. Eighty-two ticks equal C07, counted at build time and asserted 82 vs 82. On S07 the fifty evenly spaced phantom ticks ARE NSF's rationale drawn honestly, superimposed on the two states at true area, so the deformation is in one frame. The projection-note state machine turns the progress indicator into the argument. A stranger could guess the story from S02, S04 or S08 alone. Deductions: on S06 the encoding is defeated by its own rendering, the ring coil reading as ornament so the 'unequal grounds' half vanishes; on S01 the two-ring comparison fails at feed scale; S07's dimension call prints no values, so the 'two parts dimensioned to the same tolerance' reading is available only to someone who read the dossier; and Device C, the graticule edge-tease, is admitted by the pixel log as not visibly running at all.

criteria.name: Alaska authenticity & local relevance
criteria.why: Geography is accurate and load bearing rather than decorative: true lon/lat geodata, one canonical conic equal-area projection shared across both states so the comparison cannot cheat, coastline resolving the Aleutians and Southeast, and Alaska's size as the actual argument rather than a backdrop. 570,641 and 1,034 both correct and both LAND area on both sides of the ratio. The deadline is live and a reader can act on it. Deduction, and it is structural: this is a FEDERAL story with Alaska as its case study, and NOT ONE Alaska institution, place or person appears on any slide. selection.md says a reader 'at the University of Alaska, at Alaska Pacific, at Ilisagvik' can act on this and then no slide names one. Ketchikan and Utqiagvik appear only in the caption. Swap one polygon and one number and this deck is about Montana. An Alaskan would feel accurately drawn, not seen.

criteria.name: Insight density & factual weight
criteria.why: Every content slide adds a new verified specific. S01 the ratio plus the solicitation number and posting date. S02 true relative area plus ten anticipated awards. S03 three verbatim rule sentences including the enforcement half most coverage omits. S04 three distinct dollar figures with the announcement-versus-solicitation split kept explicit. S05 NSF's own problem statement. S06 both land areas and the ratio. S07 the concession plus the counter. S08 the deadline, the annual recurrence and the ceiling-versus-cliff distinction. Body counts sit in band at 30 to 38 words. The killed-claims discipline is exemplary: the $10 million average was killed as arithmetic NSF does not state, the cost-sharing overreach was narrowed to its accurate version, the per-state research university count was killed for having no source, and the total-area figure was excluded to prevent a unit mismatch that would have inflated the ratio to 643. Deduction: the 552 ratio is stated three times (cover, S06 readout, S06 sub) and S06's sub at 16 words is the deck's one thin beat.

criteria.name: Variety vs ledger
criteria.why: Checked directly against artwork.json entries 29 to 32. Hero diverges as a category change. Atmosphere at azimuth 118 sits roughly 174 degrees from the 292-to-305 band the last three decks shared, so the deck is lit from the opposite side of the sky. Hook archetype THE CONTRADICTED ARTIFACT is distinct from THE DISQUALIFYING VIRTUE, THE MEASURE THAT STOPS, No. 31's question-first and THE HONEST WITNESS. The palette is the genuine standout, PLATE NIGHT AND REGULATED MAGENTA: magenta has never been this series' accent, and the gold budget is cut from a full-strength single-meaning accent (three consecutive decks) to two sub-0.4-percent appearances. Type trio is new and retires Instrument Serif, Archivo and Unbounded. Two honest deductions. JetBrains Mono returns from the immediately preceding deck and has now been the instrument voice in four of the last six, so the plan's own aim to 'retire at least two of them' was met at two of three. And internal variety regressed on the measure the run chose to attack: median pairwise 0.329 against No. 31's 0.179 and No. 32's 0.227, drawn share 66 percent against their 100 and 99. The run set a 65 percent target BELOW its own recent shipped performance and then cleared it by one point.

criteria.name: Legibility & platform fitness
criteria.why: Every slide reads at 432px in the thumbs, body copy sets at 34px, safe zones cleared, progress counters present on all nine, vector PDF at 4.86 MB with a 37-character title, no clipping anywhere, and the deck's best legibility decision is putting art-band labels on opaque knockout plates on S04, S06, S07 and S08. Against that: the mono margin runs 20px and the kickers 22px on all nine slides, both under the rubric's stated 24px floor, and it is systematic rather than a squeaker. The knockout plates the storyboard promised under EVERY art-band label did not ship on the projection note, scale value or source line of 01, 02, 05 and 06, which sit as bare type on textured ground against the run's own 0.99 instinct. S06's ranked strip is not readable as data at any size, thumb or full. S07's source line sits adjacent to its counter with almost no gap. Three annotation elements terminate without a value.

criteria.name: Copy: voice & hook
criteria.why: Hook lands at 77 characters, well inside the fold, and it is a number rather than a tease. 869 characters, inside the 300 to 900 band. Deck-summary line present. Real analytical position taking, 'Most get nothing' and 'Alaska's ceiling was set before anyone read a proposal', with no hedging into mush. Closing question is genuinely debatable and specific to the reader who can act, 'Is 82 days enough for Alaska's institutions to line up behind one proposal?'. Clean on every brand rule I checked by hand: no first person, no colon, no 'cannot', no conjunction openers, no banned phrase, straight quotes, three hashtags at the end, no link in body. Deduction: at 869 it sits 31 characters under the ceiling and well past the 400 to 700 sweet spot, and paragraph three ('The rule counts states. Alaska counts once from Ketchikan to Utqiagvik') largely restates paragraph one, so the caption's softest 130 characters are also its most cuttable.

criteria.name: Deliverable completeness
criteria.why: Complete and well organised: post copy, exactly 3 hashtags, a first-comment source block ordered primary first with four resolvable URLs, document title, 9 renders, 9 thumbs, contact sheet, vector PDF, claims.json, aggregate report, machine_qa, assemble_report, storyboard with a synced GATE STATUS block, and a five-item aftercare checklist that is specific rather than generic (posting window with a reason, 60-second comment paste, the 48-hour save-versus-comment read as an editorial signal). The 82-day staleness is correctly surfaced in both aftercare and editor_notes_for_email. Deductions: image and PDF URLs cannot be verified from here because they point at main and the merge has not landed; site_fresh FAILs as expected pre-ship; and the storyboard's own Device B state table has drifted from the shipped strings on S01 ('ROT 154W' dropped) and S03 (rewritten), so the run record disagrees with the artifact in two rows.

threshold_basis: 2 revision rounds completed (one pixel-critic round across all nine slides, one flow-critic round on the sequence). Iteration ladder row 'revision_rounds 0-2' gives threshold 8.3. No relaxation applied.
ship_recommendation: SHIP. 8.45 against 8.3, zero hard fails. It clears by 0.15, which is the narrowest margin in the recent run of shipped decks (No. 31 at 8.42, No. 32 unscored here, No. 10 and No. 4 at 8.90), and it clears on the strength of its argument and its story-art fusion rather than on its drawing. The honesty work is the best thing in the run and should not be re-opened.
weakest_criterion: Artwork craft & genuine detail (7, weight 0.16, costing 0.48 weighted points, the largest single drag on the total)
one_sentence_fix: Split the one hachure texture that currently stands in for paper tooth, machined metal and terrain across six slides into three genuinely different materials, because a bench of eleven techniques still reads as one deck-wide surface when a single texture supplies the look on two thirds of the frames.
strengths: Factual honesty is the best in the series to date. The deck argues against NSF's stated goal using only NSF's own sentences, never says NSF is spending $100 million flat (S04 prints the announcement figure and the solicitation range side by side and leaves the volume between them unfilled), never implies Alaska has applied or been refused, explicitly states on S08 that a missed cycle is not exclusion, and keeps LAND area on both sides of the 552 ratio with the readout saying so. The killed-claims list shows six separate places the run declined an easier and wronger story.
S07 exists to make NSF's case properly before declining it, and the deck is stronger for conceding first. That is rare and it is what makes the thesis survive a hostile read.

Story-art fusion is genuinely computed rather than illustrated: one shared equal-area projection means the 552 draws itself, the 48px invariant ring is claim C01 as an object, and both the $100M scribe position and the 82-tick count are machine-asserted against their printed numbers.

S04 is the deck's best slide. The deliberately unfilled volume between two scribe lines is the most honest way I have seen a funding range drawn, and it refuses the $10 million average the fact-checker killed.
S05's hachure field and S07's Alaska relief both survive the zoom test outright, with real varied stroke width and genuine ridge and valley structure.

The pixel review log is honest in both directions. It records a refusal (the 48px ring measurement) with a grep-verified reason and files the real lesson as a Phase 12 candidate, and it records what was knowingly left rather than burying it.
The cover line is best-in-class for the platform: nine words, one number, a named tension, no jargon, legible at 432px.
weaknesses: One organic hair texture is the deck's visual signature on six of nine slides and is the wrong material on most of them, most damagingly on S04's funding casting where the dossier promised metal that 'reads machined rather than organic' and shipped the opposite.

The deck's own headline physics claim, ONE GLOBAL LIGHT at 118/26 from a single declared constant, is untrue on slides 01 and 07 because AK.reliefShade runs its own NW key. Disclosed, but the storyboard sells the single light as a structural commitment, so a reader comparing the two best slides sees the deck contradict itself.

S06's ranked strip reads as a magenta coil rather than as fifty states. The 'silhouette collapsing from Alaska to nothing' thumb read the dossier predicted does not happen; the ring row is uniform height end to end, so the picture actually says 'all fifty are the same' and loses the 'unequal grounds' half of the argument the slide exists to make. This is worse than the disclosure admits and it is the deck's declared best image.

Three annotation elements carry no terminal value: S01's leader runs off the Rhode Island ring and stops in void, S07's dimension call between the two states prints none of the values its own type spec declares, and S08's stamp leader descends and stops in bare sheet. The pixel round claimed to fix leaders on 01, 06 and 08; only 06's was actually fixed. machine_qa cannot catch this because its leader check verifies the START lands on target, not that the far end carries a label.
S07 fails its own acceptance checklist item, 'Alaska's relief mass is cut by the bottom edge, not floating above it'. It floats, above the emptiest lower band in the deck after S03.

S03's declared modelled rescue from deliberate flatness (engraved registration furniture with lit inner edges and cast shadows, ghost coastline through the band) shipped as flat 1px line art, leaving the deck's largest dead region.
The knockout plates the storyboard promised under EVERY art-band label did not ship on the margin type of slides 01, 02, 05 and 06.
No Alaska institution, place or person appears on any slide, in a deck whose own selection memo names four of them as the audience.

Two brand.yaml constellation fixtures are absent: gold #FFC72C does not appear on slides 01 through 07 (argued as a gold budget in the storyboard, but brand.yaml says 'appears deliberately on every slide'), and the coordinates footer was removed from S09 during the pixel round to clear a margin.

Internal variety regressed against the last two decks on the exact measure this run chose to attack: drawn share 66 percent versus 100 and 99, median pairwise 0.329 versus 0.179 and 0.227. The 65 percent target was set below the run's own recent performance.
editor_notes_for_email: 1) THE 82 IS PERISHABLE. The tick count on slide 08, the '82 days' headline, and both mentions in the caption are true only for a post on August 14, 2026. If posting slips even one day, slide 08 must be re-rendered and the caption re-counted to November 4, 2026. This is the single thing that would make the deck wrong rather than imperfect. 2) The deck deliberately carries NO gold on slides 01 through 07, which departs from brand.yaml's constellation rule that #FFC72C appears on every slide; the storyboard argues it as a budget (two sub-0.4-percent appearances on 08 and 09) and I did not treat it as a hard fail, but it is a standing-spec change that should be either ratified or reverted rather than left as a per-run decision. The S09 coordinates footer was also dropped during the pixel round. 3) Three annotation elements ship without their terminal labels (S01 leader, S07 dimension call, S08 stamp leader). Nobody will read them as broken, but they are visible stray lines, and machine_qa structurally cannot see this class of defect because it only checks the leader's origin. Worth a Phase 12 candidate alongside the ring-diameter assertion already filed. 4) Slide 07 shipped against a failed item on its own acceptance checklist (Alaska's relief cut by the bottom edge). 5) site_fresh FAILs as expected at this stage because docs/ is rebuilt at ship time after scoring; that row must be green before the merge. 6) Nothing in the deck claims Alaska has applied, been refused, or lacks a credible proposer, and slide 08 states in as many words that a missed cycle is not exclusion. If a commenter pushes on 'is this a scandal', the deck's own position on slide 07 is that the rule is defensible, and that reply is already written into the artwork.
